propositions: The snapshot janitor's absolute 2 GiB free-space watermark is disk-size-blind and on a 30-GiB root only engages at 93.3% used, above the 85% alarm floor and above the observed 90% peak.
The janitor's 7-day cold-trim is dead code on a container recreated multiple times daily; the byte-total backstop promised by ADR 0005 is not implemented in _gc_pass.
Every review materializes a full ~620 MiB copy of the ticket tree keyed on a ref that advances every ~26 seconds with zero reuse, driving ~4.4 GiB/h growth on the root disk.
The snapshot store lives on the container's writable layer (root disk) because REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR is unset everywhere and store_root() falls through to tempfile.gettempdir().
Garbage collection must engage at or before the 85% alarm floor, not after; a volume-relative watermark term with hysteresis restores this ordering on small volumes.
